extracted.intended_audience: conference chairs, area chairs, and reviewers (conference organizers and reviewers using TPMS)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and operational principles for using the Toronto Paper Matching System (TPMS) to build reviewer profiles, compute reviewer-paper suitabilities, and perform constrained reviewer assignment for conferences. Covers registration, profile composition, integration with conference management systems, bidding behavior, assignment objectives, and data-use terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer profile built from self-selected publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Build a profile for each reviewer using that reviewer's self-selected list of publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers may include their full set of publications or select a subset reflecting topics they wish to review; selected papers can include tech reports and notes. Registration lets reviewers keep a permanent record of selected publications and update them at any time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability scoring (profile -> reviewer-paper suitability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Using the profile we calculate the suitability of the reviewer to each submitted paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suitability scores are computed from the reviewer profile and are used to estimate how well a reviewer matches a submitted paper. The system uses these scores together with other information (e.g., keywords from CMT).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of reviewer-paper suitabilities and auxiliary info for assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewer-paper suitabilities, in addition to other information such as the keywords used in CMT, can then be used to help assign reviewers to papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suitabilities are combined with conference-provided metadata (keywords, bids/queries) to inform the assignment algorithm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment objective: maximize total suitability subject to constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: The assignment process entails maximizing the total reviewer-paper suitabilities, while satisfying certain constraints, in particular load balancing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The system optimizes a global objective (sum of suitabilities or another chosen objective) under constraints specified by program chairs (e.g., load balancing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment constraints (e.g., load balancing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignments must satisfy certain constraints, in particular load balancing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constraints placed by chairs (such as reviewer load limits, conflict avoidance, area quotas) are enforced during optimization; these constraints can cause a reviewer not to receive their highest-scoring papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guarantee: global optimality relative to chosen objective and inputs
rubrics_metrics.description: Such a constrained assignment does not guarantee that reviewers will be assigned to the papers for which they have the highest scores. The only guarantee is that the assignment will be globally optimal, for some chosen objective, given the scores and constraints set in place by the program chairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users should understand that optimality is relative to the provided scores and constraints; changing scores or constraints changes the outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer control over profile contents
rubrics_metrics.description: As a reviewer, you have the option of including your full set of publication, or to select a subset which reflects the topics of papers you wish to review for the given conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selecting a focused subset helps the system target topics you prefer; including more publications may broaden apparent expertise. Tech reports and notes are allowed as selected items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bidding used as queries to estimate suitability (not binding)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some conferences also use the service to help select papers on which reviewers and area chairs can bid on. In some cases these are not bids in the standard use of the term, but rather more like queries, in that their aim is to help the system estimate that reviewer's suitability for other submitted papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bidding highly on a paper does not guarantee assignment; bids may be treated as signals to improve suitability estimates rather than binding requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration with conference management systems
rubrics_metrics.description: The system is now integrated with several conference management systems: Microsoft's CMT and ConfMaster, and START V2 (softconf.com). This lets the system easily access conference submissions from both systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integration enables automatic ingestion of submissions, keywords, and other metadata to compute suitabilities and perform assignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data use and privacy terms
rubrics_metrics.description: We reserve the right to use any collected data exclusively for academic research purposes. We will never share collected data with third parties unless data is already publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users should be aware that data collected by TPMS may be used for academic research and will not be shared externally except when already public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer registration and persistent editable profile
rubrics_metrics.description: We ask reviewers to register on our site, and to provide a list of their own publications, which are used to create your profile for any participating conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration provides a permanent, editable profile that can be shared across conferences and updated before or between conferences.
